what: How the task view groups, orders and nests its rows — as a table of inputs and the answer `buildEntries` gives for each. A header row carries its kind, its count(s) and the ids it points at, never its title: the wording is the caller’s, the decision is the rule’s.
why: This rule lives in `shared/taskGrouping.ts` and is asked on both surfaces while rendering. It is moving into cal-core, where a Rust implementation has to give the same answer; while both exist this file is what keeps them together, and once the TypeScript goes it is the record of what the rule did on the day it moved. Written by running the TypeScript BEFORE the port, so the port is measured against what is, not against what the port thinks it should be.
writtenBy: src/components/views/taskGrouping.measure.test.ts — a one-off, run once and deleted; its table mirrors src/components/views/taskGrouping.test.ts plus the rows the port needs that that file never exercised (the two-level priority scale, list-name ordering, a task-level and a list-level collapse, a list missing from the name map, one case with everything at once).

whereItLives.note: Inside cal-core, like normalizedTitle.json and normalizeJoinUrl.json: twelve adapter repositories compile cal-core, and an include_str! reaching out of the crate would break the day it moves. A crate reads its own files.

shape.baseTask: the Task every case starts from; a case’s `tasks` entries are overrides merged over it

input.tasks: overrides over baseTask, in arrival order (arrival order must not matter)
input.lists: list id → display name; a list absent here is named and ordered by its id
input.sections: list id → Section[] as the store holds them (arrival order must not matter)
input.today: YYYY-MM-DD; the deferred gate compares against it
input.currentUserByList: list id → the connected user, for the Done mine/others split; absent = personal list
input.collapsed: ids whose children are hidden; task ids and synthetic header ids alike

expect.rows: DFS order. {id, depth, hidden, hasChildren} for every row; header rows add `group`: {kind, parentId, listId?, sectionId?, count, mine?, others?}. `mine`/`others` appear only when Done splits. `parentId` is the enclosing header’s id (null at the top). The synthetic header ids are collapse keys persisted by the UIs and must not change.

shape.language: the app language tag the answers were measured under (the collation of titles, section names and list names depends on it); the TypeScript side binds it through installTextCollation, the Rust side takes it as a parameter

cases.name: done-split-when-someone-else-owns-one
cases.note: One done task assigned to another user → the Done header splits into mine / others.

cases.name: done-single-count-when-all-mine-or-unassigned
cases.note: Unassigned counts as mine; no split without a foreign owner.

cases.name: done-single-count-without-an-identity
cases.note: No connected user for the list → everything is mine → one count, even for a task assigned to someone.

cases.name: list-mode-folds-every-open-task-into-its-list
cases.note: Backlog, scheduled and deferred all sit in their list; only Done stays separate. Lists by name.

cases.name: sections-by-name-not-by-order
cases.note: `Section.order` is creation order wearing the name of a preference; sections read A→Z. The orders are the REVERSE of the alphabet so the old rule cannot pass.

cases.name: sections-compare-numbers-like-a-human
cases.note: "Sprint 2" before "Sprint 10" — natural, not lexicographic.

cases.name: time-groups-in-order
cases.note: Überfällig → Heute → Backlog (→ its list) → Zukünftig. Future-scheduled and deferred share Zukünftig.

cases.name: zukuenftig-soonest-effective-day-first
cases.note: A scheduled day and a resurface day compete on the same axis: near (05-25) < defer (06-15) < far (08-01).

cases.name: time-groups-stay-flat
cases.note: Sections are ignored inside Überfällig and Heute.

cases.name: time-groups-count-the-whole-subtree
cases.note: parent + two subtasks = 3 on the Heute header, like Backlog.

cases.name: cancelled-gets-its-own-group-after-done
cases.note: A cancelled task with a past day must NOT land in Überfällig.

cases.name: cancelled-most-recently-changed-first
cases.note: No cancelled_at exists; updated_at stands in.

cases.name: backlog-sections-alphabetical-ungrouped-first
cases.note: Backlog(0) → Inbox(1) → Doing(2), To Do(2); the ungrouped task follows the list head directly.

cases.name: headers-count-the-contained-subtree
cases.note: a + b + b1 = 3 on both the list and the section header.

cases.name: no-sections-means-flat-under-the-list
cases.note: A section_id pointing nowhere is ignored when the list has no sections.

cases.name: done-parent-expanded
cases.note: Completed top-level tasks under a synthetic Done header, most recent first, visible while expanded.

cases.name: done-parent-collapsed
cases.note: The header stays visible, its children hide; the index space is unchanged.

cases.name: completed-subtask-stays-under-its-open-parent
cases.note: No Done group: the only completed task is a subtask.

cases.name: dfs-chain-is-strictly-nested
cases.note: Backlog(0) → Inbox(1) → To Do(2) → p(3) → c(4).

cases.name: three-level-scale-has-three-bands
cases.note: high → medium → low, A→Z inside each band.

cases.name: two-level-scale-has-two-bands
cases.note: In the two-level system only "important" floats; medium and low are one A→Z run.

cases.name: parent-cycle-surfaces-instead-of-vanishing
cases.note: a→b→a: one member is promoted to the top, the other nests beneath it.

cases.name: ordinary-trees-and-orphans-untouched
cases.note: An orphan (parent not in the snapshot) surfaces at top level.

cases.name: done-falls-back-to-updated-at
cases.note: A completion record created already-done (Vikunja) has no completed_at; updated_at is its completion moment.

cases.name: backlog-lists-order-by-name
cases.note: Two lists in the backlog read by list NAME, not by id or arrival.

cases.name: unknown-list-falls-back-to-its-id
cases.note: A list missing from the name map is named by its id — and ORDERED by it.

cases.name: collapsing-a-task-hides-its-subtree-only
cases.note: A task-level collapse: the parent stays, its children hide, its siblings do not.

cases.name: collapsing-a-list-hides-its-sections-and-tasks
cases.note: Collapse keys are the synthetic header ids; they must survive the port unchanged.

cases.name: list-mode-with-sections-and-done
cases.note: Section ids in list mode carry the `ls:` scope, in the backlog the `bl:` scope.

cases.name: everything-at-once
cases.note: One of each group, two lists, sections, subtasks, a deferred task, a done split, a cancelled task.
